world.label: World
world.description: Identify all 201 country and territory flags by name.
world.lead: Identify every country and territory flag by typing the place it represents.
world.overview: This complete set mixes flags from every part of the world, including countries, territories, and the other places used by Smurdy's world map quiz.
world.challenge: Similar color patterns repeat across continents, and several flags differ only by a symbol, stripe order, or shade.
world.studyTip: Learn one continent at a time, then return to the world set once the regional patterns feel familiar.

us_states.label: US States
us_states.description: Identify the flags of all 50 US states by name.
us_states.lead: Identify the flags of all 50 US states by typing each state name.
us_states.overview: The set includes every current state flag, from Alabama through Wyoming, including Mississippi's current magnolia flag.
us_states.challenge: Many state flags use a seal on a blue field, so small details and lettering matter more than broad color patterns.
us_states.studyTip: Learn the most distinctive designs first, then compare the similar blue-and-seal flags side by side.

europe.label: Europe
europe.description: Practice all 44 flags in Smurdy's Europe set.
europe.lead: Type the country represented by each of the 44 European flags.
europe.overview: This set covers the full Smurdy Europe group, from the Nordic countries and British Isles to the Balkans and European microstates.
europe.challenge: European flags contain many similar tricolors and crosses, so stripe direction, color order, and small emblems are important.
europe.studyTip: Group the Nordic crosses, horizontal tricolors, vertical tricolors, and emblem flags before mixing the full set.

asia.label: Asia
asia.description: Practice all 51 flags in Smurdy's Asia set.
asia.lead: Type the place represented by each of the 51 Asian flags.
asia.overview: This set spans the Middle East, Central Asia, South Asia, East Asia, and Southeast Asia. It uses every flag available from Smurdy's Asia map group.
asia.challenge: The set is large and includes several flags built from red, white, green, and black, especially in western Asia.
asia.studyTip: Split Asia into subregions, then use symbols such as crescents, suns, stars, and scripts to separate similar color schemes.

africa.label: Africa
africa.description: Practice all 56 flags in Smurdy's Africa set.
africa.lead: Type the place represented by each of the 56 African flags.
africa.overview: This set covers North, West, Central, East, and Southern Africa along with the continent's island countries and the other places in Smurdy's Africa map group.
africa.challenge: Red, yellow, and green appear across many African flags, making stripe order and central symbols especially useful clues.
africa.studyTip: Study neighboring countries together and note which Pan-African designs add a star, crest, or different stripe direction.

north_america.label: North America
north_america.description: Practice the 23 national flags in Smurdy's North America set.
north_america.lead: Type the country represented by each of the 23 North American flags.
north_america.overview: This set combines Canada, the United States, Mexico, Central America, and the sovereign Caribbean countries included in Smurdy's North America group.
north_america.challenge: The Caribbean contributes many smaller countries whose flag designs may be less familiar than the three large mainland countries.
north_america.studyTip: Learn the mainland and Central America first, then study the Caribbean flags as a separate cluster.

south_america.label: South America
south_america.description: Practice the flags of all 12 South American countries.
south_america.lead: Type the country represented by each of the 12 South American flags.
south_america.overview: This compact set includes every sovereign country in South America, making it a useful first regional flag quiz.
south_america.challenge: Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela share closely related tricolors, while several other flags also use red, white, and blue.
south_america.studyTip: Compare Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela directly, then learn the remaining nine as distinct designs.

oceania.label: Oceania
oceania.description: Practice the flags of all 14 countries in Smurdy's Oceania set.
oceania.lead: Type the country represented by each of the 14 Oceanian flags.
oceania.overview: This set covers Australia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, and the independent island countries spread across the Pacific.
oceania.challenge: Several flags share blue fields, Union Jacks, or Southern Cross stars, while the smaller Pacific nations may be less familiar.
oceania.studyTip: Compare Australia and New Zealand first, then group the Pacific designs by shared symbols and colors.
